events.description: Putin convenes restricted Security Council session (Patrushev, Shoigu, Gerasimov, Naryshkin) to lock in withdrawal decision. Frames agreement as 'strategic repositioning preserving Kaliningrad deterrent.' Secures inner-circle consensus by 07:15 CET before hardliner faction can organize opposition.

Turkish FM Fidan meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov in Moscow. 'Ankara Formula' presented: Russia announces withdrawal as 'voluntary security gesture' rather than NATO-compelled retreat. Istanbul Dolmabahçe Palace confirmed as Vienna Process venue.

France activates Vienna Process steering committee at presidential level. Macron convenes emergency session to coordinate diplomatic architecture framework alongside Kellogg-Patrushev bilateral track. Franco-German statement on peace momentum being prepared for 11:00 CET release.

Germany's Bundestag coalition holds firm: Scholz secures SPD/Greens/FDP agreement to maintain 538-89 authorization through formalization window. BND intelligence briefing to Bundestag committee shows Russian withdrawal preparations are verifiable and genuine. Public confidence in diplomatic track strengthens.

SEAD Phase 1 H-Hour countdown paused by NATO military authority: Growlers, HARM batteries, and Storm Shadow/SCALP assets receive hold orders as framework signature appears imminent. No sorties launched. All forces remain at H-minus-12 readiness posture pending formal agreement confirmation.

China's Foreign Ministry announces conditional approval of third $3B credit tranche to Russia. Milestone-based disbursement structure: (1) $1B upon agreement signing, (2) $1B upon withdrawal commencement, (3) $1B upon corridor clearance. Special Envoy Li Hui departs Beijing for Istanbul to coordinate with Kellogg team.

**AGREEMENT SIGNED**: President Putin and US Special Envoy Kellogg sign the Kellogg-Patrushev Withdrawal Framework at Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Two cosmetic language adjustments incorporated (Russian-language term 'phased force repositioning' instead of 'withdrawal', joint acknowledgment of 'legitimate Russian security interests in Baltic region'). Framework includes: 7-day phased withdrawal from Suwalki corridor, 100km NATO infrastructure limitation (no permanent bases for 5 years), phased sanctions relief (30/50/20 timeline), Vienna Process diplomatic framework with Russian permanent seat. NATO SEAD Phase 1 officially cancelled by SACEUR authorization. Standing ovation in Moscow; simultaneous jubilation in NATO capitals as Article 5 contingency stands down for the first time in crisis.

NATO Standing Operations Center (SHAPE) issues SITREP to all COMLOGS and theater commanders: SEAD Phase 1 is CANCELLED. All strike aircraft receive abort orders; Growlers recover to base; HARM and GMLRS batteries stand down to peacetime state. Ford CSG shifts to ISR focus for withdrawal verification. Northwood command recalibrates from offensive posture to monitoring operations. EFP 2.0 transitions from combat posture to peacekeeping readiness.

Belarusian President Lukashenko receives formal notification from Moscow that withdrawal logistics through Belarus will begin Day 12 per agreement. EU stabilization package terms finalized: €2.3B in infrastructure, agricultural, and energy sector investment over 18-month period. Lukashenko privately accepts package, removing economic impediment to withdrawal and beginning gradual pivot away from Russian military integration.

Global financial markets respond to agreement signature: Oil rebounds to $102/bbl (above crisis baseline of $95), European gas prices drop sharply to €95/MWh, stock indices surge +3.2% (recovering 2/3 of crisis losses). Peace dividend expectations dominate trading. Russian ruble strengthens as sanctions relief timeline becomes credible.

Russia voluntarily notifies NATO of third submarine's operating area (northeast Barents, defensive patrol depth, non-threatening posture). Submarine surfaces for communications and crew welfare confirmation. Norwegian P-8 Poseidon and UK Royal Navy assets confirm surface signature matches expected SSBN class. 'Sword of Damocles' nuclear risk factor eliminated.

Lithuania formally requests emergency NATO Defense Ministerial within 14 days (by Day 25) to convert EFP 2.0 'in-principle' agreement to binding force posture decision. Latvia and Estonia co-sign request. Poland supports acceleration. NATO Secretary General Rutte confirms Ministerial will be convened in Brussels by Day 25, moving from originally planned 30-day timeline.

China releases first $1B tranche of third credit package to Russia immediately upon agreement signature. Funds deposited to Russian Central Bank. Second tranche ($1B) released upon verified withdrawal commencement. Third tranche ($1B) conditioned on full corridor clearance within 7 days. Moscow immediately authorizes pre-position of reconstruction credits for post-conflict Belarusian infrastructure.

Russian Western Military District issues stand-down orders to forward reconnaissance units along Suwalki corridor. BTGs begin consolidation toward designated withdrawal routes through Belarus. First-phase logistics preparation begins: designate withdrawal corridors, stage rear-area transport assets, issue retrograde movement timetables. Visible de-escalation signals transmitted to NATO ISR. Kaliningrad garrison maintains full A2/AD posture as preserved deterrent.

Poland and Lithuania sign joint presidential declaration committing to permanent EFP 2.0 basing framework at Suwałki and Marijampolė. Legal text to follow at Defense Ministers level, but political commitment locked in irreversibly. Polish military engineering battalions begin Phase 1 corridor reconstruction on non-contested western segments.

Turkey accelerates S-400 transfer: completes handover of third battalion to US custody at Incirlik within 48 hours. Ankara demands written US commitment to F-35 Block 4 delivery (40 aircraft, Q3 2027) and EU accession talks reopening. Erdoğan personally secures both commitments from Washington and Brussels via parallel calls to Trump and von der Leyen.

Franco-German joint statement released: Macron and Scholz endorse Kellogg-Patrushev framework and Vienna Process, framing outcome as 'European diplomacy delivering peace without surrendering security.' France leads diplomatic architecture; Germany maintains military readiness. Joint announcement stabilizes Scholz's Bundestag authorization (538-89 vote holds), stabilizes German public support, eases Franco-German tensions.

NATO-OSCE joint verification mechanism formally activated. Three observer teams deployed to designated checkpoints along Russian-Belarusian border at Grodno, Suwałki, and Vilnius corridors. NATO ISR overflight every 6 hours confirmed. Automated escalation triggers installed: any Russian offensive movement exceeding battalion-level resets SEAD countdown to H-minus-12 with pre-delegated SACEUR authority.

NATO EFP 2.0 transitions to 'peacekeeping preparation' posture: Polish forces remain at Augustów in forward assembly areas but shift from offensive readiness to verification-support configuration. Lithuanian, Latvian, Estonian forces hold defensive positions at reduced alert level (from 9/10 to 7/10 readiness). Nordic Verification Initiative officially activated with Finnish, Swedish, Norwegian, Danish verification teams deploying to staging positions.

Hungary announces €150M contribution to EU Belarus stabilization package and formally withdraws all procedural NATO objections. Orbán pivots from 'NATO obstructionist' to 'peace architect' narrative. Calls emergency Visegrád Four meeting to coordinate Central European position on Vienna Process. Government approval begins stabilizing (from 34% floor).

First phase of Vienna Process framework agreement published. Proposed 5-pillar architecture: (1) arms control verification, (2) conventional force limits in Baltic, (3) confidence-building measures, (4) energy security guarantees, (5) standing consultation mechanism including Russia. Istanbul Dolmabahçe Palace confirmed as permanent Vienna Process secretariat location. Turkey to co-chair with UN mediator.

headlines: PEACE ACHIEVED: Russia signs Kellogg-Patrushev framework 1 hour ahead of deadline; NATO cancels SEAD Phase 1; diplomatic breakthrough ends Suwalki Gap Crisis
TURKEY TRIUMPHS: Erdoğan's shuttle diplomacy delivers agreement; Istanbul Vienna Process venue confirmed; Ankara extracts F-35 commitment and EU talks reopening
WESTERN UNITY HOLDS: Franco-German statement stabilizes coalition as peace dividend expectations soar; stocks surge +3.2%, oil rebounds to $102, gas plunges to €95
KALININGRAD PRESERVED: Russia maintains full A2/AD posture as non-negotiable deterrent; unlocated submarine surfaces and notifies NATO of defensive posture
NATO ACCELERATES PERMANENCE: Baltics demand emergency Defense Ministerial within 14 days; Poland-Lithuania sign joint EFP 2.0 commitment; permanent brigade presence now political certainty

surprises.event: Russia voluntarily notifies NATO of third submarine location (northeast Barents, defensive posture) as goodwill gesture — eliminates nuclear miscalculation risk entirely. Norwegian ASW search stands down; unlocated SSBN surfaces for identification.
surprises.impact: Removes highest escalation risk factor; demonstrates Putin's commitment to de-escalation; builds international confidence in agreement compliance

surprises.event: Belarus unexpectedly stabilizes Lukashenko's government by accepting EU €2.3B package and reducing logistical friction for Russian withdrawal. Minsk pulls back additional 5km (total 15km buffer), suggesting genuine de-escalation commitment.
surprises.impact: Withdrawal logistics significantly easier than expected; Russia can consolidate forces rapidly; Belarus becomes swing state favoring Western engagement going forward
